object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: An individual tracked in the system, identified by a person ID.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A person who works in the organization. Employees are identified via the Person reference scheme.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

object_types.name: Manager
object_types.definition: An employee with extra responsibilities. Managers are identified via the Person reference scheme.

source_references.excerpt: A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit identified by a unique department code.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: PersonId
object_types.definition: A unique identifier for a person.

source_references.excerpt: anyone in the system is a person with a person ID

object_types.name: DepartmentCode
object_types.definition: A unique code assigned to each department.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentName
object_types.definition: The name of a department, such as 'Payroll' or 'Field Operations'. Each department name is unique.

source_references.excerpt: Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

ambiguities.description: Department identification scheme: The transcript states 'Each department has a department code' and also 'no two [departments] share a name', establishing that both DepartmentCode and DepartmentName are unique. However, it is unclear which attribute is the primary identifier (reference_mode). The code is explicitly called an identifier, but the name is equally unique. Should Department be identified by department_code, department_name, or both? If both, how should composite identification be modeled?

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code. Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

ambiguities.description: Manager mandatory participation in 'manages' relationship: The statement 'A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none' confirms that a manager may manage zero departments (optional participation). However, it is unclear whether a department MUST be managed by a manager, or whether a department can exist without a manager. Is participation on the Department side mandatory or optional?

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Department mandatory participation in 'employs' relationship: The statement 'Departments have many employees' implies departments must have employees, but it is not explicit whether every instantiated department MUST have at least one employee, or whether a newly created department could initially have zero employees.

source_references.excerpt: Departments have many employees
